concerns.message: The server-side checks for a targeted rumor (design step 4: ledger state, then targetedRumorAvailability) never check that the buyer is moored at a dock. Only the journal's button is gated on 'moored at any dock'. §11 makes the shop dockside, and the constraints say the server is authoritative. A request queued at a dock and processed on a later tick after the ship cast off also passes.
concerns.consequence: Any client that sends the purchase message buys rumors anywhere at sea. The browser scenario and the listed integration tests all moor first, so the gap ships unnoticed, and economy-online's dockside shop inherits a purchase path with no location rule. Settle it by adding 'moored at a dock on the processing tick' to check 4(a), with its own recorded refusal reason and an integration test that refuses an at-sea purchase without charging.

concerns.message: 'Replay first' only covers ids that are already decided. A retry of an id that is still pending takes a second queue slot. The first copy is bought, and on the next tick the second copy passes the checks and reaches stepIntel under the same namespaced id. Intel answers 'duplicate', which the room records as a refusal.
concerns.consequence: The same (player, request id) ends up both bought and refused, and the client gets a refusal right after its delivered lead. Which record a later retry replays depends on lookup order. Deduplicate against the pending queue when a request arrives, and repeat the decided-record lookup when the request is taken from the queue.

concerns.message: Check 4(a) is a hand-written copy of the ledger's purchase rules, and a refused purchase after delivery throws and faults the whole match. The check is only safe if it runs after every ledger operation of the tick (advanceLedger, encounters, channels, settlements), which means in stepReveals just before stepIntel. The design says 'on that tick' but doesn't pin where in the tick.
concerns.consequence: If the check runs where requests are taken from the queue at the start of the tick, a grapple landing on the buyer or a settlement changing their gold in the same tick makes purchase refuse. That throws and aborts the match for all players (§12). Calling ledger purchase once as the check, just before stepIntel, and committing its returned state only if intel delivers removes both the copied rules and the throw.

concerns.message: The pre-check and the step read the same view on the same tick. After availability says rumor or sighting, the step seems able to answer 'capped' only in a corner case, and 'duplicate' only for an evicted refusal id or a queued-twice id. Acceptance 3 still lists covered, capped, none and duplicate, and the branch table forbids unreachable rows.
concerns.consequence: If the room writes a branch per intel result, the worker can't find a failing test for the capped and duplicate branches near the end and has to collapse or remove them late. Write one branch from the start: anything other than rumor or sighting is a recorded refusal.

concerns.message: The journal's 'islands you know (unlocked or not, and whether you solved the ruin)' has no data source. The room has no discovery tracking, and ruin markers with their unlocked flag are sight-filtered (MatchRoom visibility). Only the moored island's solved/unlocked state is in the private status.
concerns.consequence: A worker who sends every island's unlocked state to every player leaks remote ruin progress. The raw-frame privacy test (acceptance 5) doesn't look for it, so it passes. Define 'known' as islands whose marker the client has seen (remembered on the client) plus islands named in its own rumors, and send only the player's own solved set.

concerns.message: Several tests need exact tick alignment: three requests pending at once for 'busy', two requests in one tick, and a rumor going stale on the processing tick. They also add a 5-player sightings match and a scripted duel match, all under the 300 s integration timeout.
concerns.consequence: Requests sent from WebSocket clients can straddle a 50 ms world tick, which makes these tests flaky. The added matches may also push the suite past its budget. Use the existing pauseAt/paused test hook to line up requests, reuse the ship placement and open-ruins hooks for the sightings setup, and measure the suite's duration early.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Call the ledger's own `purchase` once, immediately before `stepIntel` in `stepReveals`, and keep its result without committing it. That call is the gold/duel/disconnect check. If intel delivers a lead, commit exactly the state it returned; otherwise throw it away and record the room's refusal. This removes the hand-written copy of the ledger's rules and the 'second purchase must succeed or the match faults' throw and its branch. The room keeps only the delivered lead per bought id and its own last-16 refusals. Add a moored-at-dock check, and deduplicate against the pending queue when a request arrives.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Write a script of about 30 lines over `packages/simulation/src/intel/property.test.ts`'s scenario generator. On each tick, for each player and type, call `targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, p, t)` and then `stepIntel` with that request, and tally the step results that follow a passing check ('rumor'/'sighting'). If 'capped' never appears and 'duplicate' appears only when an id is re-sent, the room should collapse every non-delivering result into one refusal branch before workers start. Otherwise acceptance 3 and the branch-table rule ('no unreachable rows') collide at the end. Also run the current `npm run test:integration` once to learn how much of the 300 s budget is left for the 5-player tests.
